## Parent and Child Class

A table that extends another table is called a child class, and the table it extends is the parent class. A table can be both a parent and child class both extending and providing extensions for other tables. For ex

ample, the Server table extends the Computer table and the Windows Server table extends the Server table, thus making the Server table both a Parent and Child class.

## Configuration and Asset Management Lifecycles

An asset becomes a CI (Configuration Item) when it is deployed and remains a CI throughout its lifecycle until it is returned to stock or disposed of. As illustrated in the diagram, Configuration Management and IT Asset Management are distinct, yet complementary practices.

![IMG_3dcd](images/CIS-DF_13_img_04.jpg)

> **Visual Analysis:**
> [Type: Diagram]
>
> **Diagram Title:** Asset Life-cycle & Operational Life-cycle
>
> **Structure:**
> The diagram illustrates a continuous lifecycle process divided into three distinct phases, represented by colored background zones and directional arrows.
>
> **1. Asset Management (Green Zone)**
> *   **Flow:** Requirement -> Request -> Approval -> Procure -> Receive -> Tagging -> Storage -> Deploy
> *   **Icons:**
> *   Requirement: Person icon
> *   Request: Shopping cart icon
> *   Approval: Checkmark in circle
> *   Procure: Dollar sign in circle
> *   Receive: Delivery truck
> *   Tagging: QR code
> *   Storage: Grid of four squares
> *   Deploy: Cloud with upward arrow
>
> **2. Operational Life-cycle (Blue Zone)**
> *   **Flow:** Deploy -> Storage -> Uninstall -> Move -> Upgrade -> Break / Fix -> Configure -> Billing -> Redeploy
> *   **Central Element:** CMDB (Database icon)
> *   **Icons:**
> *   Storage: Grid of four squares
> *   Uninstall: Cloud with downward arrow
> *   Move: Location pin
> *   Upgrade: Wrench
> *   Break / Fix: Flame
> *   Configure: Clipboard with pencil
> *   Billing: Dollar sign in circle
> *   Redeploy: Circular arrows
>
> **3. Configuration Managem

ent (Teal Zone)**
> *   **Flow:** Uninstall -> Dispose
> *   **Icons:**
> *   Dispose: Trash can

> ### Build
> *   **SDLC Component:** The SDLC Component is a configuration item that represents a unique development effort.
>
> ### Sell / Consume
> *   **Service Portfolio:** Hierarchical categorization of business services (Products & Services) that define business value and facilitate the management of their life cycle.
> *   **Business Service:** Published to business users and it typically underpins one or more business capabilities. Business services are often orderable by business users. Business users are able to select the desired service commitment levels via a Service Catalog.
> *   **Business Service Offering:** Stiffication of the Business Service into options, including localization/geography, pricing, availability, capability, criticality, business approval group (CHANGE), and packaging options.
> *   **Service Portfolio:** Consumable catalogable view of available business & technical products, services, commitment options, and offerings.
>
> ### Manage Technical Services
> *   **Application Service:** Logical representation of a deployed system or application stack.
> *   **Technical Service:** Technical service is linked to service owners and typically underpins one or more business services. A Technical Service may have an operational view made up of one or more Technical Service Offerings.
> *   **Technical Service Offering:** Stiffication of the Technical Service into options, including localization/geography, environment, pricing, availability, support group (INCIDENT), technical approval group (CHANGE) and packaging options.
> *   **Dynamic CI Group:** A dynamic grouping of configuration items (CIs), based on results of CMDB Groups queries

.
> *   **Configuration Item (CI):** Physical and logical components of an infrastructure that are currently, or soon will be, under configuration management.


To operationalize and maintain the health of the CMDB, ServiceNow has created three of pillars to success. At the highest level each pillar focuses on a key customer pain point.

- First is Ingestion of CMDB data: This is how the CMDB is populated and the data is identified and reconciled. Automate as much as possible the flow of data into the CMDB at a frequency that supports your stated use cases
- Second is Governance of the data: Getting the data in is just the beginning of your CMDB journey. Next is the management and upkeep of the data to maintain a healthy CMDB and gain value from the data.
- Third is Insight into the data in the CMDB: How do you visualize and utilize this data across the platform?

## MID Server:

- The MID Server (Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery Server) is deployed inside the organization’s trusted network.
- It acts as a secure bridge between the ServiceNow instance and internal systems that are not directly accessible due to firewalls or network restrictions.
- All communication between 

ServiceNow and the MID Server is encrypted.
- ServiceNow sends probes to the MID Server; the MID Server executes them and returns results, which sensors use to update the CMDB.
- Discovery is agentless and uses standard protocols:
    - WMI for Windows
    - SSH for Linux/Unix
    - SNMP for network devices
- The MID Server ensures secure, scalable Discovery without exposing internal systems to the internet.

> **✔ Key takeaway:** *ServiceNow never directly connects to internal devices—everything goes through the MID Server.*
